q8.answer: The older run is checked against production's current_tag after its window and production-deploy lock wait. If a newer SHA has already reached production, the older SHA is no longer ahead, so the run is superseded, releases the lock and is announced in #deploys. If production is still behind, the older approved run can still deploy, which is a listed known risk.

q9.answer: Outside the window, an approved run waits for the next window start while holding no lock, and no deploy starts outside the window. While another production deploy holds the production-deploy lock, the run waits behind it with no time limit set; after getting the lock it checks the window again, and if the window has closed it releases the lock and goes back to waiting for the window before the ahead check. Whether CI limits these waits is an open question, and the 72-hour limit covers approval only.

q10.answer: The measure is the canary 5xx ratio over the last minute: canary 5xx responses divided by all canary responses, from the Prometheus query in environments.md. The run evaluates it every 15 seconds for 15 minutes, starting when deploy.sh canary exits 0. Any value above 1% fails the run at once, including the first check. After the first minute, no value or a failed or timed-out query also fails the run, while in the first minute a no-value result is ignored.

q11.answer: The design says the approval is a CI manual job restricted to release-approvers, and its request names the SHA and states when the deploy window next opens, with CI recording who approved and when. How approvers are notified that a run is waiting was not decided, and whether the approval screen can show the window time is an open question, so this is only partly decided.

q12.answer: Nothing returns the environment to a known image automatically when a stable rollout fails. For staging, a failed deploy fails the run and a person decides from SSM and kubectl; for production, a failed promotion runs canary-off and a person decides. The options are rollback to previous_tag only if that is the image wanted, deploying a known-good SHA, or leaving it for the next run; automatic rollback was rejected because it goes to previous_tag, which is not the last good image that current_tag names.
